applied_items.content:
Focused next action. `chough next` SHALL print a compact action view, separate from the full `chough status` report: the objective; the current stage with its status, iteration and side-stage callers; the recorded native change with its read state, summary state, approval and correction validity, terminal evidence validity, native next action and approved-delta result; the next valid action with its reason and, when one applies, its command; the gate for the next main stage; awaiting-human gates; blockers; the checkpoint's open questions; open acceptance-blocking bug IDs with the count of other open bugs; only the referenced observations that need attention, each once: those that are not current, leaving out a superseded run, an earlier run of a case whose later run the checkpoint also references, with counts for the rest, superseded runs counted apart; the most recent checkpoint decisions, at most 5 with their total, showing the kind and reason of entries that follow the `decided:`, `rejected:` or `failed:` prefix convention and other entries whole; the latest failed observation by its recorded observation time, with the status of each bug that links it; and a pointer to each module's native lesson source with the count and bounded paths of archived SpecSync lesson bundles, without reading lesson text or tracking which bundles were folded; the bundles named SHALL be the newest 3 by recorded finalization timestamp, then directory, with an unreadable timestamp sorting oldest, the same 3 that `knowledge/index.md` links (REQ-cli-043). `chough status` SHALL report the same open questions, all of them, in its checkpoint section. It SHALL print text by default and the same fields as JSON with `--json`, and each form SHALL be at most 16384 bytes, with every list bounded, its total stated and any truncation marked. The same records SHALL give byte-identical output; ordering SHALL use recorded fields and names, never file modification times. At plan, while the native change waits for its definition approval, the next valid action SHALL name the human scope gate, opened with `chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<gate>" --drives approve` when none is open and closed with `chough checkpoint --close-gate` and the human's decision, and neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action, `specsync change approve <id> --actor <name>`, so no agent is routed to approve its own scope; an approval on authority the human gave in advance stays as REQ-cli-029 describes. Likewise at accept, neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action for the review, `specsync change review <id> --reviewer <name>`, in any field, the native summary and the gate to done included, so no agent is routed to review its own work; where they show SpecSync's next action there, it SHALL read as the human's review at the review gate. `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL derive the next valid action from the same rules and SHALL each make at most one native status read. The move into done archives the session (REQ-history-006), after which `chough next` says there is no open session and names `chough session new <key>`, exiting 0, since that is the normal state after done. A session stays open at done only while an authorized release is still ahead or unfolded inbox entries keep it open; then, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence or no native change is recorded, the next valid action SHALL name, release first, `chough stage enter release --reason "<request>"` while an authorized release is still ahead, even with inbox entries unfolded, since the session archives itself only at the move from release into done; otherwise, while inbox entries are unfolded, including after that move, it SHALL name `chough inbox fold`, then `chough doctor --fix`. It SHALL do so rather than repeat the checkpoint's next action, and SHALL NOT recommend a stage reset. A stage reset SHALL replace the checkpoint's next action. In an earlier main stage, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence and no pause, human gate or blocking bug applies, the next valid action SHALL NOT continue the stage; it SHALL say the change is archived and recommend the new cycle, a stage reset that carries a reason followed by a new native change, except at accept, where it SHALL recommend recording done first, with `chough stage advance`, which archives the session. An archived change finalized no later than the latest reset, or reached directly by one, is the previous cycle's: before done the action SHALL keep the reset's guidance and, when the next gate is refused, name `specsync change new`, never the archived refusal or another reset. With no native change recorded, a refused `refused:no-native-change` gate SHALL name `specsync change new`, not a bare status read. The next valid action SHALL guide a fresh agent through every stage (#76): right after `chough init` at intent with no criteria referenced, it SHALL say to capture or read the intent and name `hi check`, then `chough context`; at test, it SHALL name `chough cases select` and `chough cases run` for the selected cases, and `chough bug add` for a referenced case whose latest run failed with no bug, and once every referenced case's latest run passed and no blocking bug is open, it SHALL name `chough stage advance` to accept instead, the checkpoint's own next action shown as a sentence of its own; at accept while the native change is verifying, it SHALL say the human reviews next and SHALL never suggest an agent review: for a decision to ship it SHALL name `chough change ship <id> --close-gate "<gate>"` with the relay of REQ-cli-050, which runs the review as the human, ships and closes the gate only after the native ship (REQ-cli-059), so nothing under `.chough/` changes between `change check --commit` and finalize; for a decision not to ship, `chough checkpoint --close-gate` with `--verdict block`; with no review gate open it SHALL first name `chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<review>" --holds accept --drives review` and, while SpecSync's verification counts Chough's records (REQ-records-014), SHALL say to commit that gate and run `chough change check <id>` again before the ship; and the waiting action for an open review gate SHALL name the same ship. A gate close that leaves no open gate holding the current stage (REQ-cli-050) SHALL set the checkpoint's next action to the step that decision allows, and `chough next` SHALL never name itself as the next action: `chough stage advance` after an approval or the close of a gate that drives nothing, `chough change ship <id>` after a review pass, `chough stage back --to build` after a review block, and, after a `--no-native` close, recording the next action the decision calls for with `chough checkpoint --next-action`. A stage move SHALL replace a next action that a gate close set, as a reset does, with `Continue <stage>` for the stage it reaches, so the step a close named never outlives the move that carried it out and `chough next` derives the next step from the stage reached. At accept while the native change is approved or implementing, the next valid action SHALL name the review preparation of the workflow's accept step in order, `chough change check <id> --no-commit` first when the change's deltas add or modify requirements, then the affected cases, the review gate, the commit and `chough change check <id>`, and SHALL NOT show a refused gate or a bare native status read as the action; while the latest run of a case the checkpoint references is not current, as after that first check materializes the requirement text, it SHALL name rerunning those cases with `chough cases run` before it names opening the review gate. A command that `chough next` or `chough status` shows, in the next valid action, a gate or a refusal, SHALL appear whole, whatever its length: a bound is met by cutting other text, never a command. `chough status` SHALL start with the same focused summary that `chough next` gives, at most 40 lines of text and a `summary` object first in JSON, before its full report, so the next action is never buried (BUG-0023). Decisions, completed work and open questions SHALL be read from the session's story sections (REQ-records-004), and corrections and the last actor shown as REQ-history-015 and REQ-records-007 say. Trace: LIFE-3, FLOW-13, FLOW-2, LIFE-7, LIFE-1, FLOW-12, DRIVE-3, DRIVE-24.

Acceptance Criteria
- With 500 referenced stale observations, 40 awaiting-human gates and 40 blockers of 4 KiB each, 50 decisions of 4 KiB each (a checkpoint within the 1,048,576-byte cap of REQ-cli-032), 100 failed observations, 40 bugs linking the latest failure, 40 archived lesson bundles, 16 modules in the checkpoint and a native response near the parse bound, the text and JSON forms each stay within 16384 bytes, list at most 10 entries per list and state each total.
- The view lists referenced observations that are historical, removed, ambiguous (a merge left two records with that name; the row names its places) or unavailable and counts referenced current and unreferenced ones; it carries no raw native output, no observation record and no lesson text.
- The view shows the last 5 decisions newest first with the kind and reason of prefixed entries and unprefixed entries whole; the failed observation with the greatest recorded time, ties broken by the greater observation ID, with each linking bug's status; and each module's lesson source path, at most 10 with their total, with the archived bundle count and up to 3 paths, newest finalized first, matching the lesson bundles `knowledge/index.md` links.
- Two runs over the same records, and a run after file modification times change, give byte-identical text and JSON.
- `chough next` and `chough status` report the same next valid action for the same records, and each runs `specsync change status` at most once.
- After the move into done archives the session, `chough next` says there is no open session and names `chough session new <key>`, exiting 0. A session kept open at done with an archived, authenticated change gets a next valid action that names `chough stage enter release --reason "<request>"` while an authorized release is still ahead, even with inbox entries unfolded, and otherwise `chough inbox fold`, then `chough doctor --fix`; entries still unfolded after the move from release into done keep the session open, and `next` then names `chough inbox fold`. No stage reset is named. After a reset from an earlier stage the checkpoint's next action is the new-cycle text, and back leaves it unchanged.
- At intent, design, plan, build or test with an archived, authenticated change and no pause, human gate or (at test) blocking bug, the next valid action recommends the same new cycle and not `Continue <stage>`; at accept it names `chough stage advance` to done first, which archives the session.
- After a reset from done to plan, or to intent and then advance to plan, with the old change still recorded, the command is `specsync change new`, not the archived refusal or a reset; a change finalized after the reset keeps the archived guidance. With no change recorded, the plan gate's command is `specsync change new`.
- An open question recorded with `checkpoint --question`, or folded from a session inbox, appears in the text and JSON of `next`, at most 10 with its total like blockers, and in `status`; resolving it removes it from both.
- #76: right after `chough init` the action names `hi check` and then `chough context`; at test it names `chough cases select` and `chough cases run`, and `chough bug add` for an unlinked failed run; at accept while verifying it names the human review, `chough change ship <id> --close-gate` for a decision to ship and `--verdict block` for one not to, or opening the review gate first; in a project whose records SpecSync's verification counts, it also says to commit that gate and run `chough change check <id>` again before the ship; and no output at accept names `specsync change review` with an agent as reviewer; at plan with a complete draft it names the scope gate, opening it when none is open and `chough checkpoint --close-gate` for the human's decision, and no output at plan passes on SpecSync's `specsync change approve <id> --actor <name>`.
- BUG-0023: on a checkpoint with 500 referenced observations and 40 bugs, the first 40 lines of `chough status` text give the stage, the next action and its command, the open gates and the blockers, and `status --json` starts with a `summary` object holding the same next action as `next --json`.
- After a gate close that leaves no gate holding the stage, `chough next` names `chough stage advance` (approval, or a gate that drives nothing), `chough change ship <id>` (review pass), `chough stage back --to build` (review block) or `chough checkpoint --next-action` (a `--no-native` close), and never `chough next`.
- At accept with the native change approved, before its check, `chough next` names the review preparation in order, with `chough change check <id> --no-commit` first when the deltas add requirements, and no refused gate or bare `specsync change status` as the action.
- With a change ID of 120 characters, every command `chough next` and `chough status` show, the ship command included, is whole in text and JSON.
- At accept with the change verifying and the review gate open, no field of `chough next` or `chough status`, text or JSON, names `specsync change review`.
- At test with two referenced runs of one case, the earlier failed and the later passed, and every referenced case's latest run passed, `chough next` names `chough stage advance`, lists no superseded run as needing attention and lists each observation at most once.
- After a scope gate closes with the human's approval and `chough stage advance` moves plan to build, the checkpoint's next action is `Continue build` and `chough next` names no stage advance; the same holds after a gate at intent and the move to design, and after `chough change ship` into done.
- At accept with the change approved and a referenced case whose latest run is not current, `chough next` names rerunning that case before opening the review gate; once its rerun passes, it names the review gate.
- With no open session, `chough next` exits 0 with a message naming `chough session new <key>`.

Sessions in their own folders. `chough session new <key>` SHALL create `.chough/sessions/<id>/session.md` by create-new, where `<id>` is the date and the slug of `<key>` (REQ-records-003) and `<key>` is kept as an alias, with its own timeline, and SHALL point at it; `session use <id>` SHALL point at an open session by ID, alias or the bare slug when exactly one open session has it; an active pointer that holds such an alias or bare slug, as a 0.5.x pointer that an in-place migration keeps, SHALL name that session, and `chough doctor` SHALL NOT report it as `stale_pointer`; `session list` SHALL report each session's ID, aliases, stage, status (`archived` for an archived story, otherwise its stage status) and whether it is active, open or archived. A session is finished when it is at stage done or its native change is archived on HEAD, at any stage, as the archive's `finalization.json` records, read without a native read (DRIVE-16). A session SHALL close only itself, at its own move into done or with `chough session close --reason`: `session new` and `session use` SHALL NOT archive, close or change any other session, even a finished one (#207, #214). `session list`, `chough next` and `chough doctor` SHALL list each finished open session with its fix, `chough doctor --fix` (REQ-history-012), which keeps one with unfolded inbox entries or an open awaiting-human gate open and names the recovery: `chough inbox fold`, or `chough checkpoint --close-gate`, since closing a gate is a decision (#181). When `chough stage advance` moves the active session into done and its save succeeds, after the knowledge refresh of REQ-cli-043, the helper SHALL archive that session in the same command and clear the active pointer, reporting `applied.session_archive` with status `archived` and the ID; a session with unfolded inbox entries SHALL stay open with its pointer, reported as `kept_open` with the count; a session for which release is authorized at that move (a run consent or a standing preference, as `stage enter release` requires) SHALL stay open for the release, reported as `kept_open` with that reason, and SHALL archive itself the same way at the move from release into done. The step SHALL NOT undo the move into done. To archive a session, Chough SHALL write `.chough/archive/sessions/<id>.md` by create-new: the session's front matter with `stage: done` (or the stage it closed at), `stage_status: archived`, no `next`, since the session's next action no longer applies, `closed` (the UTC date) and `outcome` (`done` or `closed-without-done`), and no receipts, so the story comes first; then the story as written; then, last, a `## Receipts` section holding `receipts` as one fenced YAML block, one map per evidence entry the session holds, ordered by its observation time, oldest first, then by ID, with its `id`, `aliases` (one scalar, comma-and-space separated), `claim`, `result`, `observed` (the entry's observation time, ISO UTC, REQ-cli-017), `duration_seconds` (the run's wall-clock seconds, when known), `command`, `revision`, `environment`, `content`, `fingerprint`, `raw_log` when present, `case`, `case_digest`, `screenshot` when present and `actor` when known (REQ-records-007), so a bug whose evidence is archived keeps its verified state, which needs a pass observed after its latest failure (REQ-cli-012), and the timing report can order and time case runs read from receipts (REQ-reporting-001); readers SHALL read receipts from that section and, for a story written before it, from the front matter. In the story, What was verified SHALL give the latest receipt of each case and every receipt bound to no case, one line each (its claim, its command unless the claim already holds it, and the first 12 digits of its fingerprint, ending `^<evidence id>`) for each entry not already listed, with one line counting the earlier runs of those cases, which stay in `receipts`; a `## Bugs` section SHALL name each bug in the session's checkpoint with its title and status, linked to its record; and the story SHALL end with the Timeline and a closing line `Closed <date>: <outcome>.`, before `## Receipts`. Chough SHALL read the story back and compare it before it removes anything, and SHALL then remove the session folder, `session.md`, `evidence/` and `agent/` included, and move its screenshots beside the story (REQ-records-013), each file only under REQ-records-012; files it keeps SHALL be reported, the folder SHALL count as archived while its story exists, and `chough doctor --fix` SHALL finish the removal once they are committed. Archiving a session SHALL NOT read, move, rewrite or remove any other session's folder or story. After it, until a session is opened, `next` SHALL say there is no open session and name `chough session new <key>`, exiting 0, and `status` SHALL refuse with that message (DRIVE-13). Evidence and bug links into an archived session SHALL resolve to its story's receipts. Two branches that record work in different sessions SHALL merge without conflict. A session that cannot be read, because it is over the bound of REQ-records-001 or invalid, SHALL NOT stop `session list`, `session new`, `session use` or another session's `next`; `session list` SHALL report it with the reason and the recovery `chough session shelve <id>`, which SHALL move the folder unparsed and byte for byte to `.chough/archive/shelved/<id>/` with a `shelved.md` giving its size, SHA-256 per file, time and reason, and clear the active pointer when it named that session. Shelving SHALL never replace a file, and no reader SHALL scan `.chough/archive/shelved/` (DRIVE-14). `chough session close <id> --reason <text>` SHALL close an open session for abandoned work without a native read: it SHALL refuse with nothing changed a blank reason, a session that is archived or does not exist, and a session with unfolded inbox entries, naming `chough session use <id>` and `chough inbox fold`; otherwise it SHALL withdraw each open awaiting-human gate of that session as `chough checkpoint --clear-awaiting-human` does, one `gate-closed` entry each and no human decision, name them in its output under `withdrawn_gates`, so the story lists no gate as awaiting, add the decision `Closed without done: <reason>` and archive the session as above with outcome `closed-without-done`, clearing the active pointer when it named that session (DRIVE-16). - After an in-place migration whose machine-local pointer holds a 0.5.x session key, `next` and `status` read that session, and `chough doctor` reports no `stale_pointer`.
- A story's receipts, and its What was verified lines for them, are in observation-time order, oldest first, whatever order the session referenced them in.
- A session with three runs of one case and one manual entry archives a story whose What was verified lists the case's latest run and the manual entry, each command once, and a line counting 2 earlier runs, while `receipts` keeps all four.
- An archived story's front matter gives `stage_status: archived` and no `next`.
- `chough session close <id> --reason <text>` on a session with an open human gate writes one `gate-closed` entry for it with no decision, names it under `withdrawn_gates`, and the story lists no gate as awaiting.
- An archived story starts its body within the first 20 lines of the file, ends with `## Receipts` holding every receipt, and names each bug of its checkpoint under `## Bugs`; a bug verified by a receipt in it stays verified, and a story written with receipts in its front matter still reads.
- After the move into done, `chough next` exits 0 naming `chough session new <key>`, and `chough status` refuses with the same message.

applied_items.content:
Timing report. The helper SHALL provide a read-only timing report derived from existing records: stage segments from transitions, including iterations, back, reset, skip, pause and resume, and side-stage enter and return; case observations and repeated-run summaries; bug creation, reproduction and verification; and the native lifecycle times native SpecSync exposes. A session's `start` entry (REQ-history-002) SHALL start its first stage segment, in Cycle 1; a timeline without one, such as a migrated or older one, SHALL leave that segment's start unknown. The text report SHALL say once, in its header, that its durations are elapsed wall-clock time, and its JSON SHALL keep that label on every value; no gate-wait, segment or estimate line SHALL repeat it. It SHALL append a timestamped transition when an awaiting-human gate opens and one when it is cleared, and SHALL report active time separately from paused time and from time waiting on a human, without recording who decided or what. Every duration SHALL be labelled elapsed wall-clock time, not effort; history summaries SHALL give ranges with their sample count, labelled estimates rather than targets; a missing, unparseable or out-of-order timestamp SHALL be reported unknown, never zero. Transitions SHALL be read from each session's timeline, in open sessions and archived stories alike (REQ-history-002), and case observations, with their run times from `duration_seconds` when known, from evidence entries and the receipts of archived stories and bugs (REQ-cli-017), within the bounds of REQ-history-003; a session or story that cannot be read SHALL be named and the report marked partial. Inputs SHALL be bounded, and the report SHALL write no record. Trace: LIFE-10, DRIVE-24, LIFE-3, LIFE-6, LIFE-7.

Acceptance Criteria
- Fixture transitions with fixed timestamps for every transition kind yield the expected segments, gate records and `direct-native-write` events (REQ-history-013) start or end no segment, a `direct-native-write` event is not counted as an unrecognised kind, and paused and waiting-on-human time are excluded from active time.
- Opening a gate appends one gate-opened transition and clearing it one gate-closed transition; the report shows its waiting time, and a gate-opened record whose gate is no longer awaiting a human, with no gate-closed record, is reported closed at an unknown time.
- A missing timestamp or an end before its start is reported unknown, not zero, and fewer than three samples are reported too few to estimate.
- Running the report leaves every Chough and SpecSync record byte-identical, and input beyond its bound is reported partial.
- With one open session and three archived stories, the report gives each session's stage segments and gate waits from its timeline and each case's runs from entries and receipts; an unreadable story is named and the report is marked partial.
- No file under `.chough/history/` or `.chough/transitions.jsonl` is read.
- After `chough init`, the timing report starts Cycle 1's first segment at the `start` entry's time, a timeline without a `start` entry leaves it unknown, and the text says elapsed wall-clock once, in its header, while the JSON labels every value.
- `chough timing`'s text says elapsed wall-clock once, in its header, and no gate-wait, segment or estimate line repeats it.
